prompt: Our public REST API (a SaaS for managing event venues) has no rate limiting. Big customers hammer /v1/bookings with polling scripts and last month a runaway integration took down the API for everyone. Write a design document for adding rate limiting to the public API. Context: Python/FastAPI behind an AWS ALB, Redis available, API-key auth per tenant, team of 4 will review and implement.
assertions: Document opens with metadata (status/author/date) and a one-sentence objective
Specifies the exact 429 response contract: a typed/branchable error body shape plus rate-limit headers (e.g. Retry-After or X-RateLimit-*)
Gives client retry guidance (backoff behavior or Retry-After semantics)
Contains an open issues / open questions section with proposed resolutions instead of silently inventing unknown traffic numbers
Contains an alternatives-considered section with at least two rejected options and a stated reason each
Includes at least one editable text-based diagram (e.g. Mermaid) with source inline
Includes a rollout/phasing plan where each phase has a verification gate
Does not fabricate specific current traffic metrics not given in the prompt (any numbers are labeled as assumptions/placeholders or derived from the prompt)
